SECTION: Chapter 6 CODE OF CONDUCT FOR LSPU STUDENTS (Definition and Type of Offenses) | Article 3. Objectives The University's Mental Health Services run a program with the following objectives: • Ensure a safe, healthy, and sustainable learning environment for all students. • Use university-trained school psychologists, guidance counselors and school nurses to help those who need assistance. • Protect the rights and freedoms of people with mental health problems • Aim to improve mental and behavioral health information systems as well as evidence-based research.
Article 3. Objectives The University's Mental Health Services run a program with the following objectives: • Ensure a safe, healthy, and sustainable learning environment for all students. • Use university-trained school psychologists, guidance counselors and school nurses to help those who need assistance. • Protect the rights and freedoms of people with mental health problems • Aim to improve mental and behavioral health information systems as well as evidence-based research.

• Integrate mental health care in the essential health services; and • Collaborate with other agencies, families, and communities to improve staffing ratios and to provide a continuum of mental health services

SOURCE: LSPU_SOURCE.txt | CHUNK: pillar3_txt_chunk_682
SECTION: Chapter 6 CODE OF CONDUCT FOR LSPU STUDENTS (Definition and Type of Offenses) | Article 1. Rationale People’s academic performance, motivation to learn, level of stress, and ability to perform well in the workplace are all impacted by mental health issues, according to the LSPU-Mental Health Services Unit. This includes not only the absence of mental illness, but also the promotion of social, emotional, and behavioral health in addition to a person's overall health.
Article 1. Rationale People’s academic performance, motivation to learn, level of stress, and ability to perform well in the workplace are all impacted by mental health issues, according to the LSPU-Mental Health Services Unit. This includes not only the absence of mental illness, but also the promotion of social, emotional, and behavioral health in addition to a person's overall health.

The Laguna State Polytechnic University has an overall program vision for mental health services, which provides a common definition of mental health, the general approach to mental health, the roles that university administrators and health service officials play in implementing these services.

SECTION: Chapter 6 CODE OF CONDUCT FOR LSPU STUDENTS (Definition and Type of Offenses) | Article 6. Mental Health Services for Students University health service personnel/officials may assess students between the ages of 15 and 17 with their consent and assent, depending on their needs.
Article 6. Mental Health Services for Students University health service personnel/officials may assess students between the ages of 15 and 17 with their consent and assent, depending on their needs.

Among the offerings: • In a clinic-based setting, university preparatory evaluations are conducted by a team of psychologists, counselors, and nurses. • An assessment and mental health counseling service for people who are having serious emotional, behavioral, and interpersonal problems • Consultation and referrals to appropriate community support services, including school support, for students and their families. • Peer facilitators program that provides psychological and educational assistance to young people. • Outreach services for adolescents with complex mental health needs that may include challenging at-risk and suicidal behaviors are offered by intensive mobile youth outreach services. • To reduce the prevalence and impact of conduct disorder, school-based early intervention programs are being implemented.

trace.answer_for_eval:
The university offers the following mental health services:

1. Assessment and mental health counseling services for students with emotional, behavioral, and interpersonal problems.
2. Consultation and referrals to community support services, including school support, for students and their families.
3. Peer facilitators program providing psychological and educational assistance to young people.
4. Outreach services for adolescents with complex mental health needs, including mobile youth outreach services.
5. School-based early intervention programs aimed at reducing conduct disorder.
6. Guidance and counseling services, including individual and group counseling, case conferences with parents/students, and follow-up/referrals.
7. Evaluation by a team of psychologists, counselors, and nurses in a clinic-based setting.
8. Mental health assessments for students aged 15-17 with consent and assent.
9. Provision of free consultation funded by the university's budget.
10. Collaboration with other agencies, families, and communities to improve staffing ratios and provide a continuum of mental health services.
